sources.title: Counting Immutable Beans: Reference Counting Optimized for Purely Functional Programming
sources.version: author-uploaded IFL2019 PDF retrieved from unversioned arXiv URL; saved bytes identify exact retrieval

sources.limits: Eager reset and pure IR differ from partial variable-sized retirement. Borrowed callee protection cannot simply be removed.

hypotheses.title: Queue-empty buddy admission refinement for scalar appended Lists
hypotheses.candidate_wording: For the exact deterministic buddy implementation, a no-debt scalar append reservation may preserve all later raw-allocation admission for a declared class of initial states, despite a different intermediate growth history.
hypotheses.motivation: C04 guard handles debt, C05 observed no difference but leaves universal placement/admission unresolved.
hypotheses.minimal_change: None initially: specify symbolic allocator states and prove or refute the transformation. Any later counterexample fixture belongs to an independently authorized engineering lane.
hypotheses.prediction: Matched source content/capacity, full initial allocator state, header-first service, no reentrancy or intervening operation, and final-buffer precondition imply continuation admission agreement.
hypotheses.accept: An induction over arbitrary buddy depth and exact split/free-list order with labeled live/free blocks; explicit handling of in-place versus moving growth. A narrower theorem must name every extra precondition.
hypotheses.reject: One matched complete allocator-state trace with baseline-success/candidate-failure or different later admission; zero pending work alone cannot be used as the conclusion.
hypotheses.novelty: Potential specific allocator/service refinement, not new preallocation or a proof inferred from seed counts. Literature priority remains open; P1 concerns a different fixed workload/model.
hypotheses.distinctness: Static placement/refinement obligation, not restarting stopped ownership-model or compiler-integration experiments.

hypotheses.title: Representation-aware closed-cohort cleanup-demand certificate
hypotheses.candidate_wording: A restricted fixed-size acyclic cohort may admit a sound cleanup-demand bound that charges future scan promotion and hidden descendants before they enter a queue.
hypotheses.motivation: C02 closed potential, immortal-prefix promotion, and one-view large-root retention expose why pending_count is insufficient.
hypotheses.minimal_change: First define an offline diagnostic/proof for existing fixed-arity records and length-bounded reference Lists; no source syntax, policy change or runtime graph scan. Compiler integration is outside this lane.
hypotheses.prediction: Declared length/backing bounds plus unique allocation charges conservatively bound all future owner visits/finalizations and retained pool charges throughout the closed cohort.
hypotheses.accept: Proof includes first-mortal List promotion, shared descendants charged once, view roots, frame/chunk capacities, cache distinction, rounding and resize overlap; rejects programs exceeding declared finite bounds. No new metadata or unbounded critical-path scan.
hypotheses.reject: Undercharge in a chain with large leaf, immortal-prefix promotion, shared-DAG double counting that defeats usefulness, or allocator contiguity treated as total-byte availability. Also reject if precision requires expensive whole-program/heap analysis incompatible with simplicity.
hypotheses.novelty: Potential Minyar-specific representation/capacity certificate. Collector-sensitive space analyses and network calculus already exist; no priority claim until exact comparison to Niu–Hoffmann/Albert/CTRC plus allocator-sensitive predecessors.
hypotheses.distinctness: New mathematical obligation only; no native-model follow-on, tool execution or compiler work is requested.
